subject: Logic
title: Prosecutor's Fallacy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Prosecutor's Fallacy usable.

hook.text: "The DNA match odds are one in a million—the defendant must be guilty." Not so fast.

buildup.text: The prosecutor's fallacy confuses P(evidence|innocent) with P(innocent|evidence). They're different.

discovery.text: In a city of 5 million, a 1-in-a-million match means about 5 people match. The suspect is just one.

twist.text: This fallacy has contributed to wrongful convictions. Courts must consider the full population, not one match.

climax.text: Evidence narrows suspects but doesn't prove guilt alone. Context and base rates complete the picture.

quiz.question: What does the prosecutor's fallacy confuse?
